resumen: With the bar on your back, the torso lowers forward hinging at the hips while the knees stay almost straight. The whole range comes from the hinge.
ejecucion: Rack the bar on your traps, as in a back squat, and set your feet hip-width apart.
With knees barely bent, push your hips back and lower your torso.
Go as far as you can keep your back flat; for most people that is close to horizontal.
Come up by driving your hips forward, not by pulling with your lower back.
Start with an empty bar: the lever is long and the weight is deceptive.
matices: In the cited study, erector spinae and hamstring activity rose with load between 50 and 90 % of maximum. It is a posterior-chain exercise with little knee involvement, which makes it useful as an accessory rather than a replacement for the deadlift: far less weight moves.
